question: Which is the phase of the moon which is a full bright view of the moon, where the moon is almost perfect round in shape?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Full moon**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phase of the moon which is a full bright view of the moon, where the moon is almost perfect round in shape, is called the **Full moon**.
 
• In this phase, the entire face of the moon that is facing the Earth is illuminated by the Sun's light.
 
• The **Full moon** occurs approximately once every 29.5 days, which is the duration of a complete lunar cycle.
 
• This phase marks the midpoint of the lunar cycle, which starts with the New moon and progresses through the Waxing Crescent, First Quarter, Waxing Gibbous, Full moon, Waning Gibbous, Last Quarter, and Waning Crescent phases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **New moon** is the phase where the moon is not visible from Earth because the side of the moon that is illuminated by the Sun is facing away from Earth.
 
• The **Crescent moon** phases (Waxing and Waning) occur when only a small part of the moon is illuminated and visible from Earth.
 
• The **Gibbous moon** phases (Waxing and Waning) occur when more than half of the moon is illuminated but it is not yet a Full moon.
 
• The cycle of moon phases is caused by the relative positions of the Earth, Moon, and Sun. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/896a5352a810cf29d7293032fa61a1eb83d1264d436fc7bb053f0916431cae88.png]
